_comment: Extra prompt text for a phase-f4 CHANGE or FIX (npdev_relay_prompts.py appends it after the intent block; npdev_relay_engine.py decides which parts: `files` or `upsert` when the app needs them, and ALWAYS `more`). It lives in its OWN file on purpose: relay-prompts.json is bench-measured and the bench records its sha256, so a prompt that is not an f4 conversation stays byte-identical to what was measured. MEASURED 2026-11-12 with scripts/ai/bench/relay_f4_arm.py (the relay arm cannot do an f4 change): 5 cases x one model (nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b, free), ONE run per cell, so a smoke test of the text and not a pass rate. Run f4-run-5 on this text (file sha256 prefix 96e29bdd98b17699, measured before this note was written): 4 of 5 complete (ready, every file asked for, nothing extra) in the FIRST round -- whole model, split app, look only, data only; the model above the answer budget (upsert) was READY in round 1 with everything but npdev-config-proposal.json, so the theme was saved but not selected (the engine says so: theme-not-selected). Control, the previous f4 prompt without `more` (f4-run-4): the AI never sent a theme, page, menu or seed, did the look inside model.json, and 3 of 5 cases never reached READY. f4-run-2/-3 are not results (Gemini quota, an output cap, empty replies). NOT measured: any other model, a chat UI, a second run, a non-English ask. The Manager may pass phase f4 only if the owner accepts a one-model, one-run measurement.  string.Template syntax: $name substitutes, a literal dollar is written $$ (so a $$ref below is the JSON key $ref). `more` (2026-11-12) teaches the files that are not the model: themes, pages, menu, sample data, the theme selection. Its examples live in `examples` and tests/test_relay_prompts_f4.py runs every one through the real checker, so the text cannot teach a shape ingest refuses. `repair` / `repairPartial` (2026-11-12, bench run f4-run-2): a same-chat follow-up of an f4 change/fix gets `repair` appended (PARTIAL uses `repairPartial` instead of the measured text, which said 'send model.json and npdev-submission.json, do not send other files' and made the AI drop its page, menu and seed). Found when an AI fixed a theme contrast error by resending ONLY the theme and lost everything else. 2026-11-12 (bench f4-run-4): `more` lists the 13 colour names that exist and says to send only the colours that change (an AI invented accentHover/accentPressed and picked a warning yellow at 3.04:1); `upsert` says what to send when the model does not change (npdev-elements.json as {}), which the engine accepts since the same day when other files carry the change.
files:
This app is made of several files: the model.json above only points at the others. Here is every file you may change, as it is now:

$listing

How to answer for this app: send model.json (exactly as it is if you did not change it) and, each as its own NPDEV-FILE block, the COMPLETE content of every other file you changed or add. A new file goes under fragments/ or contexts/ and also needs its {"$$ref": "fragments/<name>.json"} entry in model.json. A file you do not send stays exactly as it is. In the NPDEV-END line, files= is the number of files you send.$locked
filesLocked: These files are also part of the app but cannot be changed from here, so leave them out: $names.
upsert:
Size: this model is too big to write out again whole in one answer, so for this task do NOT send model.json. Send only the parts you create or change, as npdev-elements.json, in place of model.json:

NPDEV-FILE npdev-elements.json
```json
{
  "upsert": { "concepts": [ (each concept you create or change, COMPLETE with all its fields) ], "flows": [ (...) ] },
  "remove": { "concepts": [ "NameOfAConceptToRemove" ] },
  "renames": [ { "from": "OldName", "to": "NewName" } ]
}
```
NPDev finds each element by its "name" and REPLACES it with yours, so a changed element must be written COMPLETE (a concept keeps every field it had), never only what changed. Everything you do not send stays exactly as it is. Leave out the keys you do not need. "upsert" and "remove" take these lists: $keys. These lists cannot be sent this way: $wholeOnly; if the change needs one of them, say so in "couldNotExpress". Use "remove" only for what I asked to remove. If the request changes nothing in the model itself (only a look, a page, a menu or sample data), send npdev-elements.json as just {} next to those files, instead of leaving it out. Still send npdev-submission.json as described above, and in the NPDEV-END line files= is the number of files you send.
more:
Beyond the model: when what I asked for needs it, you may also send any of the files below, each as its own NPDEV-FILE block with its COMPLETE content (count them in files= of the NPDEV-END line). Send them ONLY when the request needs them. Every file is checked before anything is written and one mistake means NOTHING is applied, so keep them small and exact.

1. A look: themes/<id>.json. The id is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at least 2 characters, and must be the file name. Example:
$themeExample
The only colour names that exist are: bg, surface, surfaceRaised, border, borderStrong, text, textMuted, accent, onAccent, positive, negative, warning, info (anything else, such as accentHover, is refused). Colours are #rrggbb only. With basedOn, send ONLY the colours you want to change (for a new look that is usually just accent and onAccent): the rest, status colours included, are inherited and already readable. Contrast is measured and a theme below the floor is refused: at least 4.5:1 for text and textMuted on bg and surface, for accent on bg and surface, for onAccent on accent, and for positive, negative, warning and info on surface (3:1 for borderStrong). So on a light theme the accent must be DARK (a medium green or teal usually fails: pick something like #0f6b4a, not #3aa57a), and on a dark theme it must be light. "basedOn" is an NPDev theme id (npdev-light, npdev-dark, high-contrast, retro, synth, farm ...), so you send only the colours that change; never reuse an NPDev theme id as your own id. A theme file alone changes nothing: the app keeps its old look until a theme is selected. So whenever you send a theme, ALWAYS send npdev-config-proposal.json too (also when the app is big and you send only what changed), choosing it as the starting theme; never write the selection in model.json. I will only apply it if I tick it:
$configExample
"ui.theme.name" picks the theme the app starts with; "ui.theme.choices" (value "*" or a comma list of theme ids) is what people may choose from. Nothing else belongs in that file.

2. Pages of your own: web/<name>.html, and web/<name>.css or web/<name>.svg. They are STATIC: no <script>, no onclick-style attributes, no javascript: links, in html, css or svg (a file with any of them is held back whole). Do not name a file like one the platform ships (shell.js, shell.css, info.html, model-authoring.html, theme.css is the one css that restyles every screen ...). To give a page a menu entry, send pages.json, merged by path with the entries the app already has, so send only the new ones (path is relative to web/):
$pagesExample

3. The menu: menu.json, a tree. It is MERGED with the app's menu, never replaced, so send only the new nodes. Kinds: GROUP (a header with children), BUSINESS (target is the name of a concept or panel of the model), PAGE (target is a page file relative to web/, sent now or already there). requiredRole must be a role the model declares. Other keys are ignored. Example:
$menuExample

4. Sample data: seeds/<id>.json, where id must be the file name. Example:
$seedExample
Use only concepts the model has. In a "smart" seed a value may be "$$ref:<alias>" (an alias an EARLIER record declared) or "$$gen:<generator>" with a generator from: $generators; a "raw" seed may use neither. A bulk record has "count" (or "repeatOver", not both); the whole file may make at most $maxRecords rows. "$$file:" values are not possible.

Never send config.json, scripts, JavaScript or Java files, or anything under secrets/, data/ or logs/: they are refused.

changes.why: The owner asked for a blue look.

repair: This answer is checked as a whole and NPDev keeps nothing from your earlier answer, so send EVERY file of the answer again, not only the ones with problems: model.json (or npdev-elements.json), npdev-submission.json and each theme, page, pages.json, menu.json, seed and npdev-config-proposal.json you are sending.
repairPartial:
Part of your last answer could not be used:
$errors

Send your answer again, complete, in the same format (NPDEV-BEGIN $code-$round ... NPDEV-END $code-$round files=$files): the model (or npdev-elements.json), npdev-submission.json and every theme, page, pages.json, menu.json, seed and npdev-config-proposal.json the request needs. NPDev keeps nothing from your earlier answer, so a file you leave out is lost.
